comment: Every mutant known to survive the mutation gate, one entry each, with the reason it survives. This list is the ratchet AGENTS.md section 11 asks for, and Stryker's own break threshold is only the backstop beside it: break compares one global score, so over the 1195 mutants of this scope a run needs 180 survivors to fail while the largest single file carries 140, which means deleting the tests of the largest file in the project reads 88.28 and passes. A survivor that is not on this list fails the build. The list moves in the shrinking direction on its own — an entry whose mutant a test now kills is dropped in the commit that wrote the test — and it grows only in a commit that says why, which a reviewer reads.
identity: An entry stands for one mutant, matched on file, line, column, mutator and replacement, all five exactly. Four are not enough: 187 positions of the recorded run carry more than one mutant with the same file, line, column and mutator, and this list has already carried two of them — at working-tree-status.ts 141:7 the replacement `true` was killed while `false` survived, and at bytes.ts 70:7 `lead >= 0xc2` was killed while `lead <= 0xc2` survived. Both are written in the past tense because both are now killed outright and neither is listed any more; what they illustrate is not past, because an entry that named only four fields would have excused the killed half of each pair as well. The cost of matching exactly is that an edit above a listed line moves it, and the entry then names no mutant; the gate reports that as a separate refusal rather than passing quietly, and says so in the message. When it happens, re-record the entry against a run — do not add a second one. The five are not a unique key either: 12 of the 1195 mutants share all five with another, all of them a ConditionalExpression Stryker emits twice where a compound condition is mutated once whole and once in part. None of those 12 is on this list and every one was killed, and the gate counts mutants rather than entries so its survivor count matches Stryker's.

kinds.test gap: A behavioural assertion over a value this code returns, or over the state it changes, would kill it. Closing it is test work in the folder that owns the file.
kinds.diagnostic text: Only the text of a thrown error changes. An assertion on the message would kill it, which constrains wording rather than behaviour.
kinds.not behavioural: No behavioural test can kill it: every observable answer is identical under the mutant, so what it changes is cost rather than result.
kinds.another gate: Behaviourally observable, but only from a ring the unit suite does not cover, and Stryker runs the unit suite only. Two things are required of a reason of this kind, because this is the kind whose one entry had neither, and the claim that entry made was false. First, the reason names the assertion and not only the gate: which committed file holds the thing that would move, and what about it would move. "gates:e2e is what asserts it" is exactly the shape of sentence that was wrong here, and it is unfalsifiable as written. Second, that gate has been watched failing with this mutant planted and green again with it removed, which AGENTS.md section 7 already requires of any gate used as evidence, and the reason records both outcomes. An entry of this kind is the one place in this list where nothing mechanical stands behind the sentence — the mutation gate runs the unit suite, so it cannot check a claim about another gate — which is why the claim has to carry its own measurement.

survivors.why: BRIDGE_GLOBAL_NAME becomes the empty string. No unit test reads the constant — its only consumers are src/preload/bridge.ts and src/ui/renderer.ts, neither of which has one — so the whole unit suite passes with it planted: re-measured for E01-M01-FIX-10 at 20 files and 326 tests, all passing, exit 0. gates:contract is what asserts it, and the assertion is a line of test/contract/shapes.snapshot.txt: the snapshot records the export as its literal type, `value BRIDGE_GLOBAL_NAME: "gitGraphical"`, because scripts/gates/contract.js asks the type checker what each export resolves to rather than reading the source text — so any change to the value changes the recorded type and the snapshot stops matching. Watched failing for FIX-10 with this mutant planted: `node scripts/gates/contract.js` exited 1 with three findings, and exited 0 again on the restored file. gates:e2e does NOT assert the value, although this entry said it did from the day it was written until E01-M01-FIX-10 measured it: test/e2e/window.spec.ts imports BRIDGE_GLOBAL_NAME and passes it into the page, so it looks the bridge up under whatever the contract currently says and is invariant under every change to that value — measured for FIX-10 with the mutant planted and the application rebuilt, all three end-to-end tests passed in 7.5 seconds. What gates:e2e does catch is the preload and the contract disagreeing about the name, which is a different fault and the one its own header records. The entry stays here either way: Stryker runs the unit suite only, so the mutant survives the mutation gate whatever gates:contract does with it. || LINE MOVED, 13 to 14. E01-M01-S06 added one import line to src/contracts/bridge.ts — the response type of the channel it adds — and the constant moved down by one. Only the line number changed and the reason above is unaltered; it is E01-M01-FIX-10's measurement and this lane did NOT re-take it, which AGENTS.md section 7 asks to be said rather than implied. What this lane did measure is the move itself: its run of the configured scope narrowed to src/core/page/ and src/contracts/ reported this mutant Survived at 14:35 and reported the entry at 13:35 as naming no mutant, which is the gate's own report of a line that moved.

The batching loop runs one extra time and appends String.fromCharCode() — the empty string — so the decoded text is unchanged. Measured: identical output at lengths 0, 1, 2, 4095, 4096, 4097, 8192 and 8193, either side of the 4096 batch. It is an equivalent mutant, so no verdict other than Survived can be about the mutant: across five full runs it was reported Survived four times and Killed once, over identical source, and neither a Timeout nor a Kill for it can be anything but the machine being busy. The honest verdict is that it survives. A longer timeoutMS would stop the verdict moving and belongs in a lane of its own. E01-M01-FIX-09 deleted the duplicated bounded read above this loop and the line moved from 166 to 144, where that lane watched the verdict move once more: its first session's full run reported this mutant Killed and its second session's scoped re-run of this file reported it Survived, over the same source.

prefixAt returns undefined, so every target lands in one bucket of the map. The bucket only narrows the candidates; the full twenty-byte comparison still decides, so the answers do not change. Measured: identical resolutions over 1220 lookups seeded to include hits, misses and forced prefix collisions, and the whole unit suite passes. What changes is the work done, and src/core/parse/ exposes no work counter to assert it against where src/core/store/ has storeWork and src/core/layout/ has layoutWork.
